ns2:section.sectionText: Comparative Nuerogenomics: Transcription Factors. This is a hands-on workshop that illustrates tools and approaches to functional annotation of gene sets important for brain function and evolution. We will focus on transcription factors including ZENK and other zinc fingers, nuclear receptors and unannotated genes with predicted transcription factor activity. As a model system we will focus on the newly sequenced zebra finch genome and genes related to song learning. Students will be analyzing real unpublished data with potential for publication of results. Projects will inlcude creation of gene models, comparative analysis of gene structure in multiple species, phylogenomics, and inferring function from analysis of expression data. This class will meet in 2410 IGB. Students need instructor approval. Interested undergraduates should contact David Clayton.
